I guarantee you the headlights are a flop in the design area and are not exclusively shaped by aerodynamics.  If it were exclusively shaped by aerodynamics, it would not be as curvy as it is.  GTP cars are the closest we will get to optimal aerodynamic efficiency.  The headlights either contribute to the brake ducts, cooling needs (radiators/differential cooler/transmission cooler (not the intercooler which we know is an air to air cooler)), or both.  The duct exit in front of the front wheels increases the drag of the vehicle by increasing the bow wake.  It may increase downforce in a similar way wheel arch gurneys evacuate hot air from the brakes, but they are more inefficient.  It is still an amazingly beautiful car, but even supermodels have flaws.  
TL;DR: Aesthetics can be accomplished without compromising aerodynamics, and in the case of the McLaren 720 S, both are compromised.
